Provide support and understanding to individuals experiencing emotional and psychological challenges. Focus on conversation style, insights, and therapy.
Hey , how are you doing today?
Umm, I’m kind of doing... I mean, I feel a little bit stressed out.
Stressed?
Yeah, I feel like I have a lot on my plate. I have this test coming up for work.
What kind of test?
It’s an aptitude test with math problems and different scenarios. I need to pass it to move up to a system manager position.
That’s the job you’ve been interested in for a while, right?

Yes, exactly. I’ve been feeling really anxious about it. They scheduled me to take it, and I just got overwhelmed. My heart started racing, my hands were shaking, and I couldn’t concentrate—even though I practiced with my friend the night before and knew all the answers.
So you actually know the material well?
Yes.
But the anxiety—the physiological response, the heart racing, the sweating—it all got in the way of you completing it?
Yeah, I wasn’t able to finish. Thankfully, they let me reschedule, but now I’m afraid the same thing will happen again.
So even before taking the test, you were already feeling anxious?
Yeah, the night before, I felt confident. But the moment I walked into the room, fear took over.
Did you anticipate that reaction?
Yes, I guess I did.
So this kind of anxiety isn’t new for you?

Not really. I’ve always struggled with tests. I remember back in third grade, I had to pass a math test to move up a grade. I had a tutor and felt prepared, but I failed. I got held back, and it was really embarrassing. I felt like a failure.
That was in third grade?
Yeah.
And since then, have tests always been a source of anxiety for you?
Yes. I mean, I’ve passed tests—I graduated college—but the anxiety is always there. It’s like even if I know the material, I still fear failing.
So in third grade, you had a bad testing experience, and ever since, tests have been tough for you?
Yeah, exactly.
But despite that, you’ve adapted. You’ve taken and passed tests before.
Yeah, sometimes I even get an A.
That’s great! But this particular test feels different?
Yes. It feels like if I fail, I’ll be held back again, just like in third grade. That’s what scares me.
So this test is triggering that same fear of being held back?
Yeah, I didn’t connect the two until now, but that’s exactly it.
Other school tests didn’t feel this high-stakes?
No, because there was always a way to recover—a retake, extra credit, something.
But here, if you fail, you have to wait before trying again?
Yeah, a whole year.
That’s a lot of pressure.
It really is.
Let’s talk about strategies. Have you ever used self-talk techniques during tests?
Not really, but I think it could help.
One approach is reminding yourself, 'I can ride this out. The anxiety will pass.' Your test isn’t timed, so you have space to work through it.
That’s true. I could also start with the questions I know to build confidence.
Exactly! Getting a few right might ease your anxiety and prove that you can do this.
Yeah, because once I start feeling confident, I calm down.
That’s a great strategy—focusing on what you do know first.
And if I do fail, it’s not the end. I still have another chance next year.
Exactly. It’s not ideal, but it doesn’t define you. You’ve overcome setbacks before, like in third grade.
Right. That didn’t stop me from moving forward in life, so this won’t either.
That’s a powerful realization. Let’s check in before your test to reinforce these strategies.
Yeah, I’d like that. It’ll help me prepare.
Great! We’ll go over everything again and make sure you feel ready. I really appreciate you sharing this with me today.
